doc.title: Billy Taylor interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995

title: Growing up near the Howard Theater in Washington
summary: Asked who influenced him, Taylor describes how Ellington, Basie and Lunceford played the Howard Theater beside his father's office and grandfather's church.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Tell us some of the other people that you admired their playing at the time. You say you finished college.
Yeah. I went to Virginia State College.
Okay, tell me some of the other players that you admired when you finished undergraduate. Who were you listening to at that time? Who influenced you?

Well I was lucky, I was lucky, I grew up in Washington, D.C. and in growing up in Washington, D.C., all the big bands came to the Howard Theater. My father, who was a dentist, had an office around the corner, literally around the corner from the theater. My grandfather’s church was almost adjacent to the theater. So much of my family, the things that I was legitimately in place for, was close to this theater, where all of the great artists played. Where Duke Ellington, where Count Basie, where Jimmie Lunceford, all the great players came.
